modern:
Every believer should be thirsting for God, for the living God, and longing to climb the hill of the Lord and see him face to face. We shouldn’t rest content in the mists of the valley when the summit of Tabor is waiting for us. My soul thirsts to drink deep from the cup kept for those who reach the mountaintop and bathe their brows in heaven. How pure the dews of the hills are, how fresh the mountain air, how rich the food of those who live up there, whose windows look into the New Jerusalem! Many saints are content to live like men in coal mines, who never see the sun. They eat dust like the serpent when they could taste the heavenly food of angels; they are content to wear the miner’s clothes when they could put on royal robes; tears spoil their faces when they could anoint them with heavenly oil. I’m convinced that many a believer pines in a dungeon when he could walk on the palace roof and view the good land and Lebanon.

Rouse yourself, believer, from your low condition! Throw off your laziness, your sluggishness, your coldness, or whatever interferes with your chaste and pure love for Christ, your soul’s Husband. Make him the source, the center and the circumference of the whole range of your soul’s delight. What bewitches you into such folly as staying in a pit when you could sit on a throne? Don’t live in the lowlands of slavery now that the freedom of the mountains has been given to you. Don’t be satisfied any longer with your stunted achievements, but press on to higher and more heavenly things. Aim at a higher, nobler, fuller life. Upward to heaven! Nearer to God!

modern:
Broad rivers and streams produce fertility and plenty in the land. Places near broad rivers are known for their variety of plants and their abundant harvests. God is all this to his church. Having God, she has *abundance*. What can she ask for that he won’t give her? What need can she name that he won’t supply? “In this mountain shall the Lord of Hosts make unto all people a feast of fat things.” Do you want the bread of life? It drops like manna from the sky. Do you want refreshing streams? The rock follows you, and that Rock is Christ. If you go without, it’s your own fault; if you are cramped, you aren’t cramped in him but in your own heart.

Broad rivers and streams also point to *trade*. Our glorious Lord is to us a place of heavenly commerce. Through our Redeemer we trade with the past: the wealth of Calvary, the treasures of the covenant, the riches of the ancient days of election, the stores of eternity, all come to us down the broad stream of our gracious Lord. We trade with the future too. What ships, loaded to the waterline, come to us from the millennium! What visions we have of the days of heaven on earth! Through our glorious Lord we have dealings with angels, and communion with the bright spirits washed in blood who sing before the throne; better still, we have fellowship with the Infinite One.

Broad rivers and streams are especially meant to suggest *security*. In the old days rivers were a defense. Oh, dear friends, what a defense God is to his church! The devil can’t cross this broad river of God. How he wishes he could turn the current! But don’t be afraid, for God stays unchangeably the same. Satan may worry us, but he can’t destroy us; no galley with oars will invade our river, and no proud warship will sail past.

modern:
The worst sluggards ask only for a little sleep; they’d be indignant if anyone accused them of complete idleness. A little folding of the hands to sleep is all they want, and they have a crowd of reasons to show that this indulgence is perfectly proper. Yet by these littles the day ebbs away, the time for work is all gone, and the field is overgrown with thorns. It’s by little delays that people ruin their souls. They don’t intend to put things off for years: a few months will bring a more convenient time; tomorrow, if you like, they will attend to serious things; but the present hour is so busy and altogether so unsuitable that they beg to be excused. Like sand from an hourglass, time slips away; life is wasted in dribs and drabs, and seasons of grace are lost by little sleeps. Oh, to be wise, to catch the flying hour, to use the moments as they fly! May the Lord teach us this holy wisdom, for otherwise a poverty of the worst kind awaits us: eternal poverty, which will lack even a drop of water and beg for it in vain.

Like a traveler steadily going on his way, poverty overtakes the lazy, and ruin overthrows the undecided. Each hour brings the dreaded pursuer nearer; he doesn’t stop along the way, for he is on his master’s business and must not delay. As an armed man comes in with authority and power, so want will come to the idle, and death to the unrepentant, and there will be no escape. Oh, that people were wise in good time, and would seek the Lord Jesus earnestly before the solemn day dawns when it will be too late to plow and to sow, too late to repent and believe! At harvest it’s useless to mourn that seed time was neglected. Faith and holy decision are still in season. May we gain them tonight.

modern:
No one but Jesus can set captives free. Real freedom comes only from him. It is a freedom *given with every right*, for the Son, who is Heir of all things, has the right to set people free. The saints honor the justice of God, which now makes their salvation secure. It is a freedom that has been *dearly bought*. Christ speaks it by his power, but he bought it with his blood. He makes you free, but it is by his own chains. You go free because he carried your burden for you; you are set at liberty because he suffered in your place. But though it was dearly bought, *he gives it freely*. Jesus asks nothing of us to prepare for this freedom. He finds us sitting in sackcloth and ashes, and tells us to put on the beautiful clothes of freedom. He saves us just as we are, all without our help or merit.

When Jesus sets free, the freedom is *settled on us forever*; no chains can bind us again. Let the Master say to me, “Captive, I have set you free,” and it’s done forever. Satan may plot to enslave us, but if the Lord is on our side, whom shall we fear? The world with its temptations may try to trap us, but he who is for us is mightier than all who are against us. The schemes of our own deceitful hearts may harass and trouble us, but he who has begun the good work in us will carry it on and complete it to the end. The enemies of God and man may gather their armies and come at us with concentrated fury, but if God acquits, who is the one who condemns? The eagle that soars to its rocky nest and then rises above the clouds is no freer than the soul Christ has set free. If we are no longer under the law, but free from its curse, let our freedom be *shown in practice* by our serving God with gratitude and delight. “I am thy servant, and the son of thine handmaid: thou hast loosed my bonds.” “Lord, what wilt thou have me to do?”

modern: In these words the Lord claims, as plainly as can be, the right to give or withhold his mercy by his own sovereign will. As the power of life and death belongs to the king, so the Judge of all the earth has the right to spare or condemn the guilty, as seems best to him. By their sins people have lost all claim on God. They deserve to perish for their sins, and if they all do, they have no grounds for complaint. If the Lord steps in to save some, he may do so as long as the ends of justice aren’t defeated; but if he judges it best to leave the condemned to suffer their just sentence, no one may put him on trial at their bar. Foolish and impudent is all this talk about everyone’s right to be placed on the same footing; ignorant, if not worse, are the arguments against God’s grace that makes distinctions, for they are only the rebellions of proud human nature against the crown and scepter of Jehovah. When we are brought to see our own utter ruin, how little we deserve, and the justice of God’s verdict against sin, we no longer quibble with the truth that the Lord isn’t bound to save us. We don’t grumble if he chooses to save others, as though he were wronging us; we feel that if he graciously chooses to look on us, it will be his own free act of undeserved goodness, and we’ll bless his name for it forever.

How can those who are the subjects of God’s election ever adore his grace enough? They have no room for boasting, for sovereignty shuts it out completely. The Lord’s will alone is glorified, and the very idea of human merit is thrown out in everlasting contempt. There is no more humbling teaching in Scripture than election, none that does more to promote gratitude, and so none that does more to make us holy. Believers shouldn’t be afraid of it, but should rejoice in it with adoration.

modern: “Whatsoever thy hand findeth to do” refers to works that are *possible*. There are many things our heart finds to do that we’ll never do. It’s good that they are in our heart; but if we want to be really useful, we mustn’t be content with making plans in our heart and talking about them; we must actually carry out “*whatsoever our hand findeth to do*.” One good deed is worth more than a thousand brilliant theories. Let’s not wait for big opportunities, or for a different kind of work, but do just the things we “find to do” day by day. We have no other time to live in. The past is gone; the future hasn’t arrived; we will never have any time but the present. So don’t wait until your experience has ripened to maturity before you try to serve God. Try to bear fruit now. Serve God now, but be careful how you do what you find to do: “*do it with thy might*.” Do it *promptly*; don’t fritter away your life thinking about what you mean to do tomorrow, as if that could make up for today’s idleness. No one ever served God by doing things tomorrow. If we honor Christ and are blessed, it is by the things we do *today*. Whatever you do for Christ, throw your whole soul into it. Don’t give Christ a little sloppy work, done now and then as a matter of routine; when you serve him, do it with heart and soul and strength.

But where is a Christian’s might? It isn’t in himself, for he is utter weakness. His might is in the Lord of Hosts. So let’s seek his help; let’s go forward with prayer and faith, and when we have done what our “hand findeth to do,” let’s wait on the Lord for his blessing. What we do like this will be well done, and won’t fail to have its effect.

modern: The work in Zerubbabel’s hand began with small things, but no one could despise it, for the Lord had raised up a man who would keep going until the capstone was brought out with shouts. The plumb line was in good hands. Here is the comfort of every believer in the Lord Jesus: however small the work of grace may be at the start, *the plumb line is in good hands*. A master builder greater than Solomon has undertaken to raise the heavenly temple, and he won’t fail or be discouraged until the topmost pinnacle is in place. If the plumb line were in the hand of any merely human being, we might fear for the building, but the pleasure of the Lord will prosper in Jesus’ hand. The work didn’t go ahead haphazardly and carelessly, for *the master’s hand held a good instrument*. If the walls had been thrown up in a hurry without proper supervision, they might have been out of plumb; but the chosen overseer used the plumb line. Jesus is always watching the building of his spiritual temple, so that it may be built securely and well. We are all for speed, but Jesus is for judgment. He will use the plumb line, and whatever is out of line must come down, every stone of it. That explains the failure of many an impressive work, the collapse of many a glittering profession of faith. It isn’t for us to judge the Lord’s church, since Jesus has a steady hand and a true eye, and can use the plumb line well. Aren’t we glad to see judgment left to him?

*The plumb line was in active use*: it was in the builder’s hand, a sure sign that he meant to push the work on to completion. O Lord Jesus, how glad we would be if we could see you at your great work! O Zion, the beautiful, your walls are still in ruins! Rise, glorious Builder, and make her ruins rejoice at your coming.

modern:
In Joshua *the high priest* we see a picture of each and every child of God who has been brought near by the blood of Christ, and has been taught to minister in holy things and to enter the place behind the veil. Jesus has made us kings and priests to God, and even here on earth we carry out the priesthood of dedicated living and holy service. But this high priest is said to be “*standing* before the angel of the Lord,” that is, standing to minister. This should be the constant position of every true believer. Every place is now God’s temple, and his people can serve him as truly in their daily work as in his house. They are to be always “ministering”, offering the spiritual sacrifice of prayer and praise, and presenting themselves as a “living sacrifice.”

But notice where it is that Joshua stands to minister: it is *before the angel* of Jehovah. It is only through a mediator that we poor defiled people can ever become priests to God. I present what I have before the messenger, the Angel of the covenant, the Lord Jesus; and through him my prayers are accepted, wrapped up in his prayers, and my praises become sweet as they are bound up with bundles of myrrh and aloes and cassia from Christ’s own garden. If I can bring him nothing but my tears, he will put them with his own tears in his own bottle, for he once wept. If I can bring him nothing but my groans and sighs, he will accept them as an acceptable sacrifice, for he was once broken in heart and sighed heavily in spirit. I myself, standing in him, am accepted in the Beloved; and all my polluted works, though in themselves only fit to be loathed by God, are received in such a way that God smells a sweet aroma. He is content, and I am blessed. See, then, the position of the Christian: “a priest—standing—before the angel of the Lord.”

modern:
Could there be a sweeter word in any language than “forgiveness” when it sounds in a guilty sinner’s ear, like the silver notes of the jubilee to the captive Israelite? Blessed, forever blessed be that dear star of pardon that shines into the condemned cell and gives the perishing a gleam of hope in the midnight of despair! Can it be possible that sin, sin like mine, can be forgiven, forgiven altogether and forever? Hell is what I have coming as a sinner, and there is no possibility of my escaping it while sin remains on me. Can the load of guilt be lifted, the crimson stain removed? Can the diamond-hard stones of my prison ever be loosened from their sockets, or the doors lifted off their hinges? Jesus tells me that I may yet go free. Forever blessed be the revelation of atoning love that tells me not only that pardon is possible, but that it is secured for all who rest in Jesus. I have believed in the appointed propitiation, Jesus crucified, and so my sins are at this moment, and forever, forgiven because of his pains and death in my place. What joy this is! What bliss to be a perfectly pardoned soul!

My soul dedicates all her powers to him who, out of his own unbought love, became my surety and worked out redemption for me through his blood. What riches of grace free forgiveness shows! To forgive at all, to forgive fully, to forgive freely, to forgive forever! Here is a constellation of wonders; and when I think of how great my sins were, how costly the precious drops that cleansed me from them, and how gracious the way pardon was sealed home to me, I am lost in a maze of wondering, worshiping love. I bow before the throne that acquits me; I cling to the cross that rescues me; and from now on I serve, all my days, the God made flesh, through whom I am a pardoned soul tonight.

modern:
The truth was in Gaius, and Gaius walked in the truth. If the first hadn’t been so, the second could never have happened; and if the second couldn’t be said of him, the first would have been a mere pretense. Truth must enter the soul, soak into it and saturate it, or it is worth nothing. Doctrines held only as a creed are like bread in the hand, which gives the body no nourishment; but doctrine taken into the heart is like food digested, which the body absorbs to sustain and build itself up. In us truth must be a living force, an active energy, an indwelling reality, part of the very fabric of our being. If it is *in us*, we can never part with it again. A man may lose his clothes or his limbs, but his inner organs are vital, and can’t be torn out without loss of life itself. A Christian can die, but he can’t deny the truth.

Now it is a law of nature that the inside affects the outside, as light shines from the center of a lantern through the glass. So when the truth is lit within, its brightness soon beams out in the outward life and conduct. It is said that the food of certain silkworms colors the cocoons they spin; in just the same way, the food a person’s inner nature lives on tints every word and deed that comes from him. To walk in the truth means a life of integrity, holiness, faithfulness and simplicity: the natural fruit of the principles of truth the gospel teaches and the Spirit of God enables us to receive. We may judge the secrets of the soul by how they show up in a person’s way of life. Gracious Spirit, today let us be ruled and governed by your divine authority, so that nothing false or sinful may reign in our hearts, or it will spread its poisonous influence into our daily walk among people.

modern: Mordecai was a true patriot, and so, when he was raised to the highest position under Ahasuerus, he used his high rank to promote the welfare of Israel. In this he was a type of Jesus, who on his throne of glory doesn’t seek his own interests but spends his power for his people. It would be good if every Christian were a Mordecai to the church, working as well as he can for its welfare. Some are placed in positions of wealth and influence: let them honor their Lord in the high places of the earth, and testify for Jesus before great men. Others have something far better, close fellowship with the King of kings: let them be sure to plead daily for the weak among the Lord’s people, the doubting, the tempted and the comfortless. It will be to their honor if they pray much for those who are in darkness and don’t dare come near the mercy-seat. Well-taught believers can serve their Master greatly if they use their talents for the good of all, and share their wealth of heavenly learning with others by teaching them the things of God. The very least in our Israel can at least *seek* the welfare of his people, and his desire, if he can give nothing more, will be accepted. It is both the most Christlike and the happiest course for a believer to stop living for himself. Whoever blesses others can’t fail to be blessed himself. On the other hand, seeking our own personal greatness is a wicked and unhappy plan of life; its road will be hard and its end will be fatal.

Here is the place to ask you, my friend, whether you are doing all you can to seek the welfare of the church in your neighborhood. I trust you aren’t doing it harm by bitterness and gossip, or weakening it by your neglect. Friend, join with the Lord’s poor, share their cross, do them all the good you can, and you won’t miss your reward.

modern: Gossip gives off a threefold poison, for it harms the teller, the hearer and the person the tale is about. Whether the report is true or false, this command of God’s Word forbids us to spread it. The reputations of the Lord’s people should be very precious in our sight, and we should count it a shame to help the devil dishonor the church and the name of the Lord. Some tongues need a bridle more than a spur. Many people take pride in pulling down their brothers and sisters, as if that raised themselves up. Noah’s wise sons threw a cloak over their father, and the one who exposed him earned a fearful curse. One of these dark days we may need patience and silence from our brothers and sisters ourselves; let’s give them cheerfully to those who need them now. Let this be our family rule and our personal promise: *Speak evil of no man*.

The Holy Spirit does, however, allow us to rebuke sin, and he lays down how we are to do it. It must be done by rebuking our brother to his face, not by abusing him behind his back. This course is manly, brotherly and Christlike, and with God’s blessing it will do good. Does the flesh shrink from it? Then we must lean harder on our conscience and hold ourselves to the job, so that by letting sin stay on our friend we don’t become partners in it ourselves. Hundreds have been saved from gross sins by the timely, wise and loving warnings of faithful ministers and fellow believers. Our Lord Jesus has set us a gracious example of how to deal with friends who go wrong, in his warning to Peter, the prayer he offered before it, and the gentle way he put up with Peter’s boastful denial that he needed such a warning.

modern:
This anointing oil was much used under the law, and what it stands for is of first importance under the gospel. The Holy Spirit, who anoints us for all holy service, is indispensable to us if we want to serve the Lord acceptably. Without his help our religious services are only an empty offering, and our inner experience is a dead thing. Whenever our ministry lacks unction, what miserable stuff it becomes! And the prayers, praises, meditations and efforts of ordinary Christians aren’t one bit better. A holy anointing is the soul and life of godliness; its absence is the most painful of all disasters. To go before the Lord without anointing is like some ordinary Levite pushing himself into the priest’s office: his ministrations would have been sins rather than services. May we never attempt holy exercises without sacred anointings. They drip on us from our glorious Head; from his anointing, we who are like the hem of his robe receive a plentiful unction.

Choice spices were blended with the perfumer’s finest art to make the anointing oil, to show us how rich all the influences of the Holy Spirit are. Every good thing is found in the divine Comforter. Matchless comfort, unerring teaching, undying life, spiritual energy and divine holiness all lie blended, with other excellences, in that sacred eye salve, the heavenly anointing oil of the Holy Spirit. It gives a delightful fragrance to the character and person of the man on whom it is poured. Nothing like it can be found in all the treasuries of the rich or the secrets of the wise. It can’t be imitated. It comes from God alone, and it is freely given, through Jesus Christ, to every waiting soul. Let’s seek it, for we may have it, and may have it this very evening. O Lord, anoint your servants.

modern: This seemed a very important question to the king of Judah, and perhaps it weighs even more with the tried and tempted Christian. Losing money is never pleasant, and when principle requires it, the flesh isn’t always ready to make the sacrifice. “Why lose what could be put to such good use? Can’t even the truth be bought too dearly? What will we do without it? Think of the children, and our small income!” All these things and a thousand more would tempt the Christian to reach out his hand for dishonest gain, or to hold back from acting on his conscience when doing so means serious loss. Not everyone can see these matters in the light of faith; and even among the followers of Jesus, the doctrine of “we must live” carries quite enough weight.

*The Lord is able to give thee much more than this* is a very satisfying answer to the anxious question. Our Father holds the purse strings, and what we lose for his sake he can repay a thousand times over. Our part is to obey his will, and we can be sure he will provide for us. The Lord will be no man’s debtor in the end. Saints know that a grain of heart’s ease is worth more than a ton of gold. Whoever wraps a threadbare coat around a good conscience has gained a spiritual wealth far more desirable than anything he has lost. God’s smile and a dungeon are enough for a true heart; his frown and a palace would be hell to a gracious spirit. Let the worst come to the worst, let all the talents go, we haven’t lost our treasure, for that is above, where Christ sits at the right hand of God. Meanwhile, even now, the Lord makes the meek inherit the earth, and he holds back no good thing from those who walk uprightly.

modern: War will always rage between the two great powers until one or the other is crushed. Peace between good and evil is impossible; even pretending to have it would in fact be a victory for the powers of darkness. *Michael will always fight*; his holy soul is grieved by sin and won’t put up with it. Jesus will always be the dragon’s enemy, and not in a quiet way but actively, vigorously, fully determined to wipe out evil. All his servants, whether angels in heaven or messengers on earth, will and must fight. They are born to be warriors; at the cross they make a covenant never to make a truce with evil. They are a warlike company, firm in defense and fierce in attack. The duty of every soldier in the Lord’s army is to fight against the dragon every day, with all his heart and soul and strength.

*The dragon and his angels won’t turn down the fight*; they never stop their attacks, and they spare no weapon, fair or foul. We are foolish to expect to serve God without opposition: the more zealous we are, the more sure we are to be attacked by the henchmen of hell. The church may grow lazy, but her great enemy doesn’t; his restless spirit never lets the war pause. He hates the woman’s seed, and would gladly devour the church if he could. Satan’s servants share much of the old dragon’s energy, and are usually a busy lot. War rages all around, and to dream of peace is dangerous and useless.

Glory be to God, we know how the war ends. The great dragon will be thrown out and destroyed forever, while Jesus and those who are with him will receive the crown. Let’s sharpen our swords tonight, and pray the Holy Spirit to strengthen our arms for the battle. Never was a battle so important, never a crown so glorious. Every man to his post, you warriors of the cross, and may the Lord crush Satan under your feet shortly!
